summary: SSE reconnect splits UTF-8 codepoint leading to truncated closing paragraph for long-tail clients
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after an SSE reconnect sequence their transcript is missing the last paragraph. The missing data is not an entire token but rather a truncated UTF-8 codepoint boundary which causes the client JSON parser to drop the trailing sentence.

Impact:
- Some long responses (multi-paragraph) are missing final punctuation/characters and the client shows an abruptly cut sentence.
- Affects Veridian Health's integration (enterprise tier) for clinical note generation; customers observe data loss in ~0.7% of long sessions.

Environment:
- Prod traffic through our us-west edge cluster, requests originate from a third-party web app using the JS SDK behind an enterprise reverse proxy.
- Observed with both redwood-rlhf-1 and open-llama-13b model selections.

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Client opens SSE connection via SDK to /v1/streams with a very long prompt expecting multi-paragraph output.
2) After ~18–30s the enterprise reverse proxy triggers a reconnect (circuit change / keepalive probe).
3) SDK attempts to resume via connect+offset header; the server responds with resume chunks but the first chunk after resume ends on a half codepoint.
4) Client-side JSON parse fails to append the last segment; UI shows truncated closing sentence.

Observed behavior:
- Resume chunk boundary ends in the middle of a two-byte or three-byte UTF-8 sequence (we see 0xC2/0x82-like split bytes).
- Server-side logs show resume-offset matched and resume acknowledged, but the bytes streamed to the client contain a split codepoint at the chunk boundary.
- Browser JS SDK error: "Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input" or silent drop depending on consumer.

Expected behavior:
- Resume boundaries must align to stream JSON token boundaries or ensure the SDK seamlessly reassembles UTF-8 codepoints across resume chunks. No truncation of human-readable text.

Relevant traces/logs:
- trace_id: trace-20260310-7f4a (see logs/edge/traces/trace-20260310-7f4a.link)
- Edge proxy logs show keepalive probe and connection handoff: /var/log/edge/proxy/2026-03-10-keepalive.log#L124-L147
- SDK client dump attached as attachment: client-dump-VERIDIAN-03-10.txt
reproduction_steps: Open a long-generation SSE session from within the enterprise proxy (replicate Veridian's proxy settings)
Simulate the proxy idle probe so the client reconnects after 18-30s
Observe server resume response and capture raw bytes at resume boundary (tcpdump or edge trace)
Attempt to parse resulting streamed JSON in browser; note any SyntaxError or dropped trailing text

comments: 2026-03-10T15:02:11Z - Support (Aisha Kumar): Acknowledged. Assigned to runtime on-call for triage. Please attach a client-side HAR or tcpdump if available.

2026-03-10T15:34:05Z - Eng (Tom Reynolds): Reproduced locally by replaying a captured resume response. Confirmed chunk boundary ends with 0xC2. Hypothesis: edge proxy chunking changes byte grouping during keepalive handoff.

2026-03-11T09:12:33Z - Customer (Veridian Health - Lisa Chen): We can reproduce reliably when our gateway performs a half-close during probes. Attached a sample trace. This is blocking our daily clinical exports.

2026-03-11T11:27:44Z - Eng (Tom Reynolds): Added instrumentation to the resume path to emit boundary-safe flushes. Creating a small experimental patch to ensure resume chunks finish codepoints before sending. PR referenced below.

investigation_notes: Reproducer: replaying exact bytes from edge trace reproduces client JSON parse failure in both Chrome and Firefox.
Edge behavior: proxy sometimes coalesces or splits payloads when TCP connection is handed off; this can split multi-byte UTF-8 characters across two sends.
SDK behavior: SDK naive chunk-concat expects character boundaries to be preserved; it does not guard against partial UTF-8 codepoints across resume boundaries.
Hypothesis: combination of proxy-induced chunking + resume semantics yields half codepoints, server lacks codepoint boundary padding before ack of resume.
Test patch: runtime now pads resume responses to ensure last byte ends on a UTF-8 character boundary before emitting resume ack (branch: runtime/fix/resume-utf8-boundary)
Staging run: applied patch to staging edge group; verified 10k resumed sessions with no truncation observed in synthetic test harness.
resolution: Workaround provided to customer: increase proxy keepalive timeout or disable half-close probe for critical streams. Engineering patch merged to runtime (PR 1720) to ensure resume responses are UTF-8 boundary-safe. Plan: rollout to canary on 2026-03-13, full rollout 2026-03-15 after monitoring. Post-incident task: add unit test for resume boundary and SDK hardening to accept partial codepoints across chunk joins.
